object_description: interlocking composition of a school and a sports building linked by a canopy around a central atrium
geometry_property: ring of classrooms around the atrium
design_condition: the interlocking placement continues the volumetric structure of the neighbouring care centre and defines a sequence of spatially precise outdoor spaces that route through the middle of the complex

positive: The interlocking placement continues the volumetric structure of the neighbouring care centre
It defines a sequence of spatially precise outdoor spaces
This sequence of squares routes through the middle of the complex and anchors it in the neighbourhood
The open wide green belt contrasts with the spatially defined outdoor spaces close to the school
The hard court and playground form the central square with the buildings
The lawn extends the park strip behind the school
A wide flight of stairs opposite the main entrance provides an interior prelude inviting people to linger
The centrally lit atrium is the heart of the building, accessed by sculpturally designed staircases
Ground floor uses are all accessed independently from the entrance area
Classrooms are arranged like a ring around the atrium with two clusters per floor
Room niches for checkrooms and common areas overlook the atrium
In the sports building each use is separately accessed from a shared entrance foyer
Non-load-bearing partitions can connect to the facade in a 1.25 metre grid, ensuring maximum flexibility
Size, space efficiency and a simple load-bearing structure promise relatively low construction costs
The building impresses with rational organisation and versatile access areas
The atrium holds all parts of the organism together and ensures easy orientation
A valuable contribution characterised by great care at all levels of scale
negative: The angled canopy calls the tectonic logic of the facades into question and is not convincing
A more differentiated zoning of the dense tree planting would be desirable for permeability
The access and bicycle stand positioning have an obscuring effect on entrance and schoolyard
The connection to the existing building to the south-east is unresolved with visible terrain edges
The atrium spaciousness and atmosphere are more reminiscent of a technical college than an elementary school
The facade expression does not seem appropriate to its use
